description: FRENTE B, vector 4/3 — the Furey Cℓ(6) charge operator, and the decisive state-level test that the G₂ automorphism φ is NOT a family symmetry. Executed over Gaussian integers ℤ[i]. The Furey one-generation construction (ℂ⊗𝕆 → Cℓ(6)): left-mult L_a on the octonion (8-dim), ladder
comments: FRENTE B, vector 4/3 — the Furey Cℓ(6) charge operator, and the decisive state-level test that the
G₂ automorphism φ is NOT a family symmetry. Executed over Gaussian integers ℤ[i].
The Furey one-generation construction (ℂ⊗𝕆 → Cℓ(6)): left-mult L_a on the octonion (8-dim), ladder
operators α_i = ½(−L_{a_i} + i L_{b_i}) for pairs (1,2),(3,4),(5,6). Scaling by 2 gives Gaussian-integer
matrices M_i = 2α_i = −L_{a_i} + i L_{b_i}. This test certifies:
(1) the Witt relations {M_i, M_i†} = M_i M_i† + M_i† M_i = 4·I  (the ladder ops are a genuine Cℓ(6));
(2) the scaled charge D = 12·Q = Σ_i M_i† M_i is built (Q = ⅓ Σ α_i†α_i);
(3) DECISIVE: the G₂ automorphism φ = (e₁e₂e₃)(e₅e₆e₇) [from sedenion_gresnigt_octonions] does NOT
commute with D: [P_φ, D] ≠ 0. Since P_φ e_j = e_{g(j)} with g=(1 2 3)(5 6 7), one has
(P D)[r][c]=D[g⁻¹(r)][c] and (D P)[r][c]=D[r][g(c)], so a single index comparison witnesses it.
(4) the one-generation charge multiplicities (Fock, ×3): 3Q ∈ {0, 1×3, 2×3, 3}.
MEANING (honest boundary). A family symmetry must PRESERVE charge (map generations at equal charge).
φ does not commute with the charge ⟹ φ does NOT act as a charge-preserving (family) symmetry on the
fermion states — even though φ permutes the three octonion subalgebras. This rules out THIS φ (a G₂,
color-side element; see sedenion_gresnigt_octonions.md) as a bridge from the zero-divisor monomial-168
to fermion generations, now at the STATE level, not just by the G₂/Brown group theory. It does NOT

binary64 max-finite for any unbiased exponent e > 1023. That contradicts the

comments: indep_dsep_forged_literal_madaros
Regression for a live defect (merged, then fast-followed): `indep_dsep`
used to take `proof: i64` and compare it to the literal 1, so a hand-typed
`indep_dsep(1)` was accepted identically to a discharged
`indep_dsep(d_separated(A, B | Z))` witness -- there was no such thing as a
forged proof, because both reached the function as the same value with the
same type. See indep_dsep_forged_literal_lean_single.sio for the other
engine's variant of this same test.
On Madaros the fix is a real opaque type: `proof: DsepProof`, where
`DsepProof` names no `struct { ... }` anywhere in the tree, so no source
text can construct one via a literal, and `types_compatible` (compat.sio)
makes it compatible with nothing but itself. `indep_dsep(1)` therefore
fails the ordinary, structurally-guaranteed argument-type check -- E009,
not a dedicated diagnostic, because there is nothing dedicated to fail:
an i64 can never satisfy this parameter, for any value.
`requires: madaros` because the diagnostic is a genuine engine difference:
lean_single has no comparable opaque-type mechanism and rejects this same
program a different way (E257, a syntactic check over the witness the
compiler itself produced) -- see the lean_single-only sibling file.

error-pattern: argument type does not match parameter

comments: This was tests/known-gaps/units/derived_unit_dropped_by_inference.sio, a
reproduction of a gap that is now CLOSED (2026-09-05). It used to PASS: a
quotient lost its dimension, so mol/cm3 + K compiled. It is here, and not
there, because a file that must be refused belongs with the other refusals.
What closed it: the dimension is carried through `*` and `/` (dim_add /
dim_sub at the multiplicative site) and the additive check compares it. Both
backends carry it, so this is refused under --target aarch64-linux too --
which is what scripts/ci/a64_compile_fail_parity_gate.sh now asserts for this
file along with the rest of the corpus.
